Maya — thanks for the callout and for the traces. I pulled the signal and can confirm we saw measurable p99 degradation tied to a kernel selection change that rolled to a subset of capacity during the Nov 1 maintenance window. Engineering traced elevated memory pressure for long sequences which triggered slower kernel fallbacks for a narrow model/sequence-length combination.

Immediate steps we’ve taken:
- Rolled back the kernel selection change for the affected model variant (completed 10:45 PST).
- Enabled a conservative KV cache key partitioning to reduce memory pressure for long sessions.
- Spin up a temporary burst pool to shift affected traffic (completed 10:55 PST).

We expect baseline p99 to normalize within 1–2 hours of the rollback; we’ll monitor 24 hours and provide a post-mortem. I’m looping in Lauren and Marcus to coordinate a customer-facing remediation and commercial proposal.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand this is impacting production. I’ll follow up with a remediation note and a proposed commercial offset for your finance team to review.

Best,
Aditya

Subject: Proposal: "Performance Warranty Offset" for Stellara (requires exec sign-off)

Team — summary and proposed concession for executive approval. I spoke with Maya and Stellara leadership; they experienced user-visible degradation for ~18 hours across a production cohort. The contract's SLA has a p99 latency SLO and a financial remedy clause for sustained breaches. Stellara is a strategic mid-market account (Deal DEAL-7832), recently onboarded to Dedicated with predictable throughput.

Proposed one-off remedy (non-standard bundling; asking Marissa for sign-off):
- Credit: 15% invoice credit applied to Stellara's Nov invoice (one-time, non-recurring).
- Capacity: One month complimentary Dedicated Burst (up to 12 vGPU-hours/day) to stabilize production traffic patterns while they finish migration.
- Engineering hours: Up to 10 billed SE hours (waived) to assist with load shaping and runbook hardening.
- Conditions: Stellara signs the attached acknowledgement of remedial actions and accepts a short-term operational change log for the account (DocuSign link provided).

Rationale: a pure percentage credit feels insufficient; mixing a capacity buffer + SE time materially reduces churn risk and restores confidence. The combined financial impact is roughly equivalent to a 15–18% credit depending on usage, but the operational value to the customer is greater.

Attachments: proposed-credit-memo-stellara-20261104.pdf, latency-runbook.pdf.
Related: SUP-9876 (Jira).

Approvals requested:
- Marissa: exec approval for credit + complimentary capacity (this is an exception to standard credit thresholds).
- Marcus: confirm finance/ledger path and whether a credit memo or invoice adjustment is preferred.

If we have sign-off, I’ll prepare the DocuSign and coordinate a customer call to finalize acceptance.

Thanks,
